record.tranche_reason: The study trains image classifiers on randomly flipped labels and reports test accuracy and the training trajectory of probabilities assigned to flipped labels. These results bear on noisy-label learning, but it does not run the original fully random-label or unstructured-input experiments.
record.gate_note: The study tests label noise only up to 50%, with clean test labels. It does not report zero training error on completely random labels, test error at chance, or results for shuffled or Gaussian-noise inputs. The label-noise experiment and the Figure 4c trajectory are the study's own results; cited findings about memorizing random and corrupted labels are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own cross-entropy training trajectory shows early suppression followed by later memorization of corrupted labels, bearing on V6. Figure 4 also measures clean-test error across corruption rates, bearing on the test-error component of V4, although the supplied text contains no readable absolute curve values.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the relevant experiments: horizon loss improves top-1 accuracy under a flat learning rate, its relative gain grows with label noise, and it suppresses corrupted-label probability late while cross-entropy continues memorizing noise.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a remaining-learning-horizon loss and compares it with cross-entropy on label-noise experiments; does not reproduce the original random-label memorization method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported top-1 gain over cross-entropy rises with label noise. The flipped-label probability trajectory differs between cross-entropy and the horizon loss.

fits_no_version.finding: The horizon-loss top-1 advantage over cross-entropy grows from 3.3 to 7.3 points on ImageNet and from 0.1 to 2.7 points on MNIST between 10% and 50% corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed loss's relative clean-test advantage increases with label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: The horizon loss reduces corrupted-label probability late in training to about one-third of cross-entropy's final value.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A shrinking-horizon loss suppresses late noisy-label memorization relative to cross-entropy.

record.problems: The noise sweep reaches 50%, not fully random labels. The reported noise-sweep text gives gains over cross-entropy rather than absolute test errors, and does not report training error. The trajectory result tracks flipped-label probability but provides no corresponding true-label trajectory. The study reports no significance tests; SEM reflects variation across seeds, and it notes that three-seed ±2 SEM is only a rough guide.
record.rows_left_out: No further eligible results for the tested versions were extracted. The paper cites prior work on memorizing random and corrupted labels, but those are not this study's results.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios for real versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
All shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, and Gaussian-noise input conditions.
Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep, corruption beyond 50%, and test error reaching chance.
Random-label fitting under explicit regularization and generalization after removing regularization. The clean-label weight-decay control does not establish these.
A directly measured shared-pattern or true-label trajectory paired with the corrupted-label trajectory; completely random labels; ordering across other architectures and noise rates.

missing.what: Absolute clean-test error by corruption rate for each model and loss in Figure 4a,b. These curves measure V4's test-error component, but method gains cannot recover their direction or smoothness. No V4 verdict is justified from the supplied numerical text.

record.verdict_notes: Corruption replaces selected labels with uniformly chosen wrong classes and is fixed across methods and seeds. The original V4 limits_scope label mistakes missing measurements for contrary evidence; the original V6 limits_scope label similarly treats an unmeasured true-label trajectory as a demonstrated limitation.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random training-label condition; no reported training error or test error at chance for that condition.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed as the fraction of corrupted labels changes.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
Tests label noise only from 0% to 50%, not all labels random. Reports test-error trends and gains, but not perfect training-set fit or test error reaching chance.
No random-label fit experiment with or without weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation, and no test of removing these as a cause of poor generalization.
Tracks probability assigned to flipped labels on MNIST at 30% noise, but does not report a matching trajectory for true labels or a completely random-label condition.
